english_retrieval.snippet: ### Download App. NewsIndiaWhy BJP is facing Rajput anger in Gujarat over Parshottam Rupala's remarks. # Why BJP is facing Rajput anger in Gujarat over Parshottam Rupala's remarks. ## Union Minister Parshottam Rupala's remarks on Kshatriyas sparked massive protests by the Rajput community in Gujarat. For the past one week, the Saurashtra region in Gujarat has been on the boil, with the BJP witnessing massive protests by the influential Rajput community over Union Minister Parshottam Rupala's remarks on Kshatriyas. Despite multiple apologies by Rupala, the BJP's candidate from Rajkot, the protests have refused to die down. The streets of Rajkot have seen protesters from the community, which has always rallied behind the BJP in the state, carrying banners and shouting slogans demanding that Rupala be pulled out of the Lok Sabha race. Rajya Sabha MP Parshottam Rupala stoked a controversy on March 22 after he said at a Dalit event that the erstwhile 'maharajas' broke bread with the British and also married off their daughters to them. On March 29, Rupala again apologised in public with folded hands at a gathering of Rajput community leaders in Gondal town of Rajkot. However, the apologies have failed to cut ice with the Rajputs, who have urged the BJP to withdraw Rupala's candidature or face defeat in the May 7 Lok Sabha election. ### HOW HAVE THE RAJPUT COMMUNITY RESPONDED. The community has vowed to burn Rupala's effigy in every district if he was not removed as Lok Sabha candidate. However, the Rajput community leaders have clarified that they were only against Rupala and had no issues with the BJP replacing him with another Patidar candidate. ### HOW WILL THE ROW IMPACT THE BJP IN GUJARAT POLLS? The anger among the Rajputs has been simmering for some time now amid allegations that the community was being sidelined within the BJP. In the BJP, there are only five MLAs and one Rajya Sabha MP from the Rajput community from the Saurashtra region. Gujarat's Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel and Union Ministers Mansukh Mandaviya and Rupala are from the Patidar community. Kshatriya leader Vasudevsinh Gohil, meanwhile, said the community was capable of changing the poll results.

In the viral video, the woman's father-in-law is seen repeatedly striking her with sticks in full public view. BJP MP Mukesh Rajput's sister Reena Rajput was thrashed by her in-laws. A case of alleged assault and harassment of the sister of Farrukhabad BJP MP Mukesh Rajput has come to light in Uttar Pradesh’s Etah district, after a video of the incident went viral on social media. Police have registered a case and launched an investigation. In the viral video, the woman’s father-in-law is seen repeatedly striking her with sticks in full public view. In her written complaint to the police, she alleged long-term domestic violence and said her in-laws have been trying to drive her out of the household. Reena claimed her father-in-law and brother-in-law secretly filmed her while she was bathing. When she objected, she was beaten with the butt of a rifle by her father-in-law. She further alleged that as she attempted to escape, her brother-in-law attacked her with an iron rod on the street, leaving her wounded. The complainant, identified as Reena Rajput, has been married in Rani Avantibai Nagar of Etah for 17 years. "I have two daughters, so my in-laws beat me up. They have been torturing me for a long time and for some reason they want to get rid of me," complainant Reena Rajput, sister of BJP MP Mukesh Rajput, alleged. She further claimed that when the bad treatment by her in-laws did not bear any fruit, they filmed a video of her when she was having a bath. They beat me a lot with sticks and lathis (canes) and also beat my daughter," Reena said. Following the circulation of the video online, police registered a case under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Police confirmed that investigations are underway. "A case has been registered, and the matter is being investigated. Appropriate action will be taken as per the findings,' a senior police officer said.

Title: Among 22 new ministers in Rajasthan govt, 6 Raje loyalists & BJP nominee for delayed Karanpur poll
## 17 new faces in Bhajanlal's council of ministers, including former MPs Rajyavardhan Rathore and Kirodi Lal Meena. **New Delhi:** The newly-elected Bharatiya Janata Party government in Rajasthan added 22 leaders to the state ministry Saturday, with 12 of them being sworn in as cabinet ministers, five as ministers of state (independent charge) and five as ministers of state. The new inductees to Chief Minister Bhajanlal Sharma’s council of ministers include former MPs Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore and Kirodi Lal Meena and four MLAs who are among loyalists of former Chief Minister Vasundhara Raje Scindia, in what is being seen as an attempt to mollify the disgruntled former CM ahead of the the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. In a new twist, among Saturday’s Rajasthan ministry inclusions are Surendra Pal Singh, the party’s candidate for the 5 January polls for the Karanpur seat. Talking about the ministry inclusion, a senior BJP leader speaking on condition of anonymity told ThePrint, “the council of ministers has been made to reward the common workers of the party, most of those included in the ministry are those who have not served as minister before. After the BJP came to power in the state, winning 115 of the 199 seats and defeating the incumbent Congress, the party chose Brahmin leader Sharma as the CM to lead the government in the state. It also chose  Diya Kumari, a Rajput, and Prem Chand Bairwa, a Dalit leader, as deputy CMs. A senior BJP leader from Rajasthan had earlier told ThePrint that Sharma’s choice as CM was political necessity because of “competing caste interests” in Rajasthan. Talking about Singh’s inclusion in the ministry, a BJP leader from Rajasthan told ThePrint that “under the Constitution there is clear provision of inducting any person as minister and that the person would then have to be elected within six months. With the new inductees, CM Bhajanlal Sharma’s council of ministers now includes three Rajput leaders  Diya Kumari, Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore and Gajendra Singh Khimsar. ***Also read:*** *BJP’s social engineering in Rajasthan — why the party chose Bhajanlal Sharma as CM*.

english_retrieval.snippet:
Title: Shivraj finally picks ministers — top BJP man, 2 Scindia loyalists among 5 to aid Covid fight
HomePoliticsShivraj finally picks ministers — top BJP man, 2 Scindia loyalists among... # Shivraj finally picks ministers — top BJP man, 2 Scindia loyalists among 5 to aid Covid fight. ## Shivraj Singh Chouhan has expanded his cabinet after nearly a month, in which time MP has been struggling to contain the spread of the novel coronavirus. File image of Madhya Pradesh CM Shivraj Singh Chouhan and fellow BJP leader Narottam Mishra | Photo: ANI. File image of Madhya Pradesh CM Shivraj Singh Chouhan with Narottam Mishra (right) | Photo: ANI. **New Delhi:** Having managed Madhya Pradesh without a cabinet for 29 days, Chief Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan has finally added five ministers, and left scope for a larger expansion after the Covid-19 crisis has passed. The five ministers sworn-in Tuesday are BJP heavyweight Narottam Mishra, former ministers Kamal Patel and Meena Singh, and two former Congress ministers who rebelled against previous CM Kamal Nath and resigned their MLA posts — Tulsi Silawat and Govind Singh Rajput. ThePrint takes a look at each of the new ministers’ past record. Mishra is credited by BJP insiders as the man behind ‘Operation Kamal’ to topple Kamal Nath’s government. Mishra is a five-time MLA, and once former CM Babulal Gaur was forced into retirement, became the second-in-command to Chouhan in his previous term as CM. He has served as a minister since Uma Bharati’s time as CM in 2003, and once handled the health portfolio as well. Well-known as a political manager and someone with clout in the vernacular press, Mishra was disqualified for three years on charges of paid news by the Election Commission, but Chouhan did not drop him due to his clout. Patel has previously served as revenue and medical education minister under Chouhan. Singh is a tribal woman leader and a five-time MLA. She has served under three BJP CMs — Uma Bharati, Babulal Gaur and Chouhan — as minister for women and child development, tribal affairs and rural development. Silawat, a Jyotiraditya Scindia loyalist, was the health minister in the Kamal Nath government, and was among the first lot of MLAs to rebel against him. Another Scindia loyalist, Surkhi MLA Rajput was the revenue minister under Kamal Nath.

File image of Madhya Pradesh CM Shivraj Singh Chouhan with Narottam Mishra (right) | Photo: ANI. **New Delhi:** Having managed Madhya Pradesh without a cabinet for 29 days, Chief Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan has finally added five ministers, and left scope for a larger expansion after the Covid-19 crisis has passed. The five ministers sworn-in Tuesday are BJP heavyweight Narottam Mishra, former ministers Kamal Patel and Meena Singh, and two former Congress ministers who rebelled against previous CM Kamal Nath and resigned their MLA posts — Tulsi Silawat and Govind Singh Rajput. ThePrint takes a look at each of the new ministers’ past record. Mishra is credited by BJP insiders as the man behind ‘Operation Kamal’ to topple Kamal Nath’s government. Mishra is a five-time MLA, and once former CM Babulal Gaur was forced into retirement, became the second-in-command to Chouhan in his previous term as CM. He has served as a minister since Uma Bharati’s time as CM in 2003, and once handled the health portfolio as well. Well-known as a political manager and someone with clout in the vernacular press, Mishra was disqualified for three years on charges of paid news by the Election Commission, but Chouhan did not drop him due to his clout. Patel has previously served as revenue and medical education minister under Chouhan. Singh is a tribal woman leader and a five-time MLA. She has served under three BJP CMs — Uma Bharati, Babulal Gaur and Chouhan — as minister for women and child development, tribal affairs and rural development. Silawat, a Jyotiraditya Scindia loyalist, was the health minister in the Kamal Nath government, and was among the first lot of MLAs to rebel against him. Another Scindia loyalist, Surkhi MLA Rajput was the revenue minister under Kamal Nath.
